Hidden Waterfalls in West Bengal You Must Visit

West Bengal is not only famous for tea gardens, mountains, and culture—it is also home to several breathtaking hidden waterfalls surrounded by forests, hills, and peaceful landscapes. Many of these waterfalls remain unexplored, making them perfect for travelers seeking nature, adventure, and photography spots.

1. Changey Waterfall

Located near Lava in Kalimpong district, Changey Waterfall is one of the most beautiful hidden waterfalls in North Bengal. Surrounded by dense forests and rocky cliffs, the waterfall creates a peaceful atmosphere away from city crowds.

Why Visit

  • Crystal-clear mountain water
  • Dense green surroundings
  • Perfect for photography and nature lovers

Best Time to Visit

Monsoon and post-monsoon season

2. Buxa Jayanti Waterfall

Hidden deep inside the Dooars region, this waterfall offers a stunning blend of forest, hills, and river landscapes.

Highlights

  • Located near Buxa Tiger Reserve
  • Excellent trekking route
  • Ideal for adventure travelers

3. Paglajhora Falls

Paglajhora Falls is a famous hidden waterfall located on the route between Siliguri and Darjeeling. The name means “mad stream” because of its powerful water flow during monsoon.

Best Experience

  • Scenic road trip views
  • Foggy mountain atmosphere
  • Monsoon photography spot

4. Suntalekhola Waterfall

Suntalekhola is a peaceful eco-tourism destination known for its small waterfalls, hanging bridge, and forest beauty.

Why Travelers Love It

  • Calm natural environment
  • Riverside cottages nearby
  • Perfect for relaxing trips

5. Rambi Waterfalls

Situated near the Teesta River, Rambi Waterfalls offer breathtaking roadside views while traveling through Kalimpong.

Special Features

  • Beautiful valley scenery
  • Great stop during road trips
  • Refreshing mountain environment

6. Ambootia Waterfall

This lesser-known waterfall is surrounded by tea gardens and misty hills, making it a hidden paradise for travelers.

Best For

  • Nature photography
  • Quiet escapes
  • Tea garden exploration

Travel Tips for Visiting Hidden Waterfalls

  • Visit during monsoon or after monsoon for maximum water flow
  • Wear comfortable trekking shoes
  • Carry waterproof bags for electronics
  • Avoid slippery rocks during heavy rain
  • Start early for better photography light

Why You Should Explore These Waterfalls

Unlike crowded tourist attractions, these hidden waterfalls provide peaceful surroundings, untouched natural beauty, and authentic travel experiences. From the forests of Dooars to the hills of Darjeeling and Kalimpong, West Bengal offers countless scenic waterfall destinations waiting to be explored.
